statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Overnight Nasdaq-100 futures are reported sharply higher after NVIDIA's earnings-call reversal, but persistent no-retracement NQ structure is not yet verified.
recommendation: Tail remains in the WATCH band while the delayed NVIDIA second leg carries into overnight futures; the blocking threshold requires stronger evidence of persistent mean-reversion failure.
headline: NVIDIA follow-through lifts Nasdaq futures; Tail remains WATCH pending price-path confirmation
body: NVIDIA's post-earnings reversal has broadened into a reported roughly 1%-1.2% rise in Nasdaq-100 futures and stronger Asian technology trade. This confirms directional follow-through, while the available public evidence still does not establish repeated failed retracements or a persistent no-reversion NQ path. Oil is extending declines, reducing one cross-asset stress channel.

lookbackSummary: Across the prior 24 clock-hours, Tail stayed low through most of Wednesday, moved to WATCH after NVIDIA's post-release dip reversed sharply during the earnings call, and remained in WATCH as the delayed second leg carried into overnight trading.
outlookSummary: Residual NVIDIA repricing remains the immediate risk window. If overnight gains retrace and two-way trade returns, Tail should fall below WATCH; a separate conditional risk window develops around Thursday's 12:30 UTC claims and advance trade/inventory releases and the U.S. cash open.

forecast.analysis: Observed overnight follow-through remains strong after NVIDIA's earnings-call reversal, with Nasdaq-100 futures reported about 1%-1.2% higher. The move is directional confirmation, but public evidence still does not establish repeated failed retracements or a persistent no-reversion NQ path.

forecast.analysis: Residual earnings repricing remains capable of extending during thin overnight liquidity. Tail stays in WATCH conditionally unless retracements deepen and directional efficiency fades.
As the initial earnings impulse ages, Tail eases if futures begin to trade two-way. Continued extension with shallow pullbacks would keep the delayed second-leg mechanism active.
European pre-open liquidity should test whether the overnight technology bid is absorbed. Broader confirmation across semiconductors and index futures would be required to re-elevate Tail.
With more distance from the earnings call, residual volatility should decay unless Europe reinforces the same directional path. Conflicting cross-asset signals would favor normalization.
European cash trade becomes the main checkpoint. Tail remains low if gains rotate or retrace rather than extend efficiently across technology and megacaps.
The earnings impulse is older and no major U.S. release is due in this hour. Risk depends on whether semiconductor strength broadens into persistent index-level continuation.
Approaching the U.S. premarket, fresh participation can either validate or fade the overnight move. Tail rises only if NQ shows sustained directional efficiency with weak retracements.
U.S. premarket liquidity can amplify the prior AI impulse. WATCH would require a stronger one-way path than the current evidence base supports.

The 12:30 UTC U.S. claims and advance trade/inventory cluster approaches. Event concentration raises Stress; Tail reaches WATCH only conditionally because the release outcome and subsequent price path are not yet observed.

The 12:30 UTC data window is imminent. Conditional Tail is highest if the release triggers aligned NQ extension with shallow or failed retracements; otherwise Stress can be high without persistent Tail.
This hour contains the scheduled 12:30 UTC data releases. The future reaction is unknown; WATCH assumes only conditional risk of directional repricing, not an observed post-release trend.
After the releases, the U.S. cash open becomes the next checkpoint. Persistent opening-auction continuation with weak pullbacks would keep Tail in WATCH; orderly two-way trade would lower it.
Once the opening impulse is absorbed, Tail falls below WATCH if price discovery remains two-way. Continued session-extreme holding would be the main invalidation.
Mid-morning conditions should normalize unless macro repricing broadens across yields, semiconductors and megacaps. Conflicting signals would keep Tail low.
With the major morning catalysts behind the market, the base case is lower Stress and more normal price discovery unless a new geopolitical or policy shock emerges.
Early U.S. afternoon trade has no scheduled Tier-1 catalyst. Tail remains low unless directional efficiency reappears with repeated extension.
As liquidity shifts toward late-session positioning, mild Tail sensitivity returns if the index holds near an extreme and breadth aligns.
Power-hour approach can magnify an established trend. Conditional Tail remains below WATCH unless persistent directional structure is already visible by then.
Late-session liquidity raises conditional WATCH risk if NQ is already one-way with shallow retracements. Without that evidence, this remains a Stress window rather than a block signal.
Cash-close positioning can produce sharp moves, but Tail falls below WATCH absent persistent directional efficiency into the close.
After the cash close, event intensity should decline. Futures can remain sensitive to earnings and policy headlines, but sustained one-way structure is not assumed.

The Jackson Hole symposium backdrop remains relevant, though Chair Warsh's keynote is not until Friday. Overnight Tail stays low unless fresh price-path evidence re-establishes directional persistence.
Into the next overnight cycle, the base case is normalization. Any renewed WATCH state would require fresh persistent NQ structure or a new material catalyst.
